title: Show repertoire: Margie, Bugle Blues and marches on the bally
summary: Tunes remembered from the shows, Lee's saxophone feature, and the marches played only outside on the bally, including Shouting Liza.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: All right. Anything else about the tunes that they would do? You mentioned a few of them already.
"Margie." That's one, yeah. "Margie." "Last Night On The Back Porch."
"Last Night on The Back Porch"?

Yeah. "I kissed her or something on the back porch." [SINGS] That's the name of it, "Last Night On The Back Porch." The main one they used to play in them days was "Bugle Blues." That was the one that Lee used to feature
Phillips - 29
with
the saxophone.
That was on that first tour on the carnival show.
No.
No.
They played that on the carnival show, too. They played that on both shows. But I mean, that's the one they used to have the saxophone feature on, was "Bugle Boy."
Did you do any marches when you were in that first carnival show?
No.
No marches. They never played any marches. But you Prez you said was doing marches before you joined the band.
Marches?
Yeah. You said that he learned to improvise by playing on marches.
No, but we used to play those. We used to play those on the bally.
Excuse me?
When we come out on the ballyhdo, make the ballyhoo, go to the bally. When they'd say, "All on!" -- that means we'd come out in front to draw the people in there.
Oh, that was in the beginning, before they went inside the tent.
Yeah.
Phillips - 30
I see. So you played marches outside.
Yeah.
but you didn't play them up inside in the carnival show.
Oh, no.
Just on the outside.
And at certain kinds we'd play... We'd play that one because that was a jazzin' march, too.
Which one?

"Shoutin' Lies."(?) It had a lot of... You could get on to that trio down there, you could tear it up. Anybody could. You could play that. You could use that for a dance tune. I think somebody did write... One band out there (who was it?), somebody had an arrangement on it.
"Baby Won't You Please Come Home" you mentioned.
Yeah.
You mentioned "Way Down Yonder In New Orleans."
Yeah.
Any other tunes that you can mention?
